title: the approve step seconds on a loaded runner: the FHIR libraries built for the load were in no named step
note: basis 'shown' means shown by reading the code, by a clock spy under CPU load in a session container, and by the card's unit test; the CI failure itself was not reproduced.

findings.claim: Compiler.approve built the FHIR libraries for the load (fhirhelpers_source() opening the translator's jar, the CQL and ELM encoded) after the compiler.files lap and before the mark of compiler.fhir_load, so that time went to compiler.unaccounted; it is the only unnamed span that reads a file, and the only one that grew under CPU load (14 to 19 ms against at most 1 ms)

the 0.79 s of compiler.unaccounted on CI job 138429378648 was a blocked read of the translator's jar or a full garbage collection in a long-lived worker while the libraries were built; not reproduced in a session container (0 of 40 runs under 16 busy processes, a cold page cache, a 3-million-object heap)
